newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Revoz union holds one-hour stike.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Revoz union holds one-hour stike.

text.p: Trade unionists at car maker Revoz, the Slovenian unit of France's Renault, held a one-hour strike on Monday, claiming conditions had worsened since Renault announced the closure of a plant in Belgium.

"Pressure on workers has greatly increased since then, working hours are being extended, while those who take sick leave are being threatened that they may lose their job," union leader Janez Jaksa told Reuters.

In February, Renault, which is a 54-percent owner of Revoz, announced it would close the Belgium Vilvoorde plant due to low car sales in Europe. The Slovenian state owns the other 46 percent of Revoz.
Production at Revoz, which employs some 2,600 people, rose to 31,120 cars in the first four months of 1997 from 30,974 cars in the same period last year.
The union said it was also pushing for higher salaries although it had yet to produce details of its demands.
Jaksa said an average net monthly salary of a worker in the production unit amounted to some 50,000 tolars ($325), well below the Slovenian average of 88,010 tolars.
Revoz management were not immediately available for comment.
The strike took place amid a 10-day train strike, which began last Tuesday and has blocked most railway traffic in the former Yugoslav republic.
